rows.name: Image Converter
rows.title: Image Converter | GXA Toolbox
rows.description: Detect and convert verified image formats locally with explicit quality, transparency, animation, and metadata handling. Use it with GXA Toolbox.
rows.intro: Universal Image Converter detects image bytes before decoding, validates dimensions and memory limits, and re-encodes pixels locally into an output format that is genuinely available. It does not treat a filename extension as proof of format support.
rows.howTo: 1 Choose one image up to 50 MB; the converter inspects its bytes, then validates the decoder and decoded pixel dimensions Choose one image up to 50 MB; the converter inspects its bytes, then validates the decoder and decoded pixel dimensions. 2 Review detected format, dimensions, file size, transparency, and any first-frame, first-page, or browser-codec limitation Review detected format, dimensions, file size, transparency, and any first-frame, first-page, or browser-codec limitation. 3 Choose an available output, set lossy quality when shown, and choose a background before converting alpha to a format without transparency Choose an available output, set lossy quality when shown, and choose a background before converting alpha to a format without transparency. 4 For animated GIF or multi-page TIFF input, explicitly confirm that only the first frame or first page should be converted For animated GIF or multi-page TIFF input, explicitly confirm that only the first frame or first page should be converted. 5 Convert, compare the preview and measured result details, then download the new file Convert, compare the preview and measured result details, then download the new file.
rows.faq: Which inputs are actually supported? Fixture-backed inputs are JPEG/JPG/JFIF, PNG, WebP, GIF, uncompressed 24/32-bit BMP, baseline uncompressed RGB/RGBA TIFF, PNG-compressed ICO/CUR, a restricted static SVG subset, and AVIF only when the current browser validates and decodes the file. Recognized formats without a verified decoder are reported as unsupported. Can it convert HEIC or HEIF? Not in this build. HEIC/HEIF is detected, but there is no fixture-verified local HEIF decoder, so the tool returns an explicit unsupported message instead of uploading the image or extracting a low-quality thumbnail. Can it convert camera RAW or Photoshop files? No. RAW files require demosaic and camera color interpretation, while PSD/PSB composite decoding requires a separate verified codec. These formats are recognized but not advertised as supported. What happens to an animated GIF? The decoder detects multiple GIF frames and requires you to confirm first-frame-only conversion. This tool does not claim to preserve animation; use GIF Frame Extractor when separate composed frames are needed. What happens to transparency? PNG, WebP, TIFF, and ICO outputs retain the decoded alpha channel. JPEG, BMP, and this GIF output path require transparent pixels to be filled with white, black, or a chosen color. Does conversion preserve metadata? No. The browser decodes visible pixels and the destination encoder creates a new file, so EXIF, GPS, ICC profiles, comments, and other source metadata are removed. A misleading preserve toggle is not shown. Why was my SVG rejected? The local SVG rasterizer accepts only a restricted self-contained static subset. It rejects scripts, event handlers, style blocks, entities, embedded documents, external or data URLs, animation, and unsupported elements to avoid executing uploaded markup. Does conversion resize images? Normal outputs keep the decoded source width and height. ICO is the deliberate exception because you choose one square icon size between 16 and 256 pixels. Where is my image processed? The bytes and decoded pixels remain in the browser workflow. Image bytes, filenames, metadata, and pixels are not sent to analytics; only the existing generic lifecycle status events are recorded.

rows.name: GPS Map Camera – Geotag Photo
rows.title: GPS Map Camera & Geotag Photo Online | GXA Toolbox
rows.description: Add a professional visible location stamp and, for JPEG output, standard GPS EXIF metadata. Use it with GXA Toolbox.
rows.intro: GPS Map Camera – Geotag Photo creates a professional visible location stamp and can write standard GPS EXIF coordinates into a JPEG. A visible stamp is part of the rendered pixels; EXIF GPS is machine-readable metadata. An uploaded photo can be assigned any location by its user, so neither form is independently certified evidence of where that photo was originally captured.
rows.howTo: 1 Upload a supported photo or explicitly allow camera access and capture one in the browser Upload a supported photo or explicitly allow camera access and capture one in the browser. 2 Use current location, search, click or drag the map marker, reuse existing GPS, or enter decimal latitude and longitude Use current location, search, click or drag the map marker, reuse existing GPS, or enter decimal latitude and longitude. 3 Review and correct the address, date, company details, optional logo, template, map size, and coordinate format in the live preview Review and correct the address, date, company details, optional logo, template, map size, and coordinate format in the live preview. Small maps use 18% of the photo’s shorter edge. 4 Choose a visible stamp, JPEG metadata only, or both; read the precise-location notice and create the output Choose a visible stamp, JPEG metadata only, or both; read the precise-location notice and create the output. 5 Download and inspect the new JPG or visible-stamp PNG Download and inspect the new JPG or visible-stamp PNG. GPS metadata modes use JPEG. Keep the untouched original, especially when replacing or removing metadata.
rows.faq: Does this prove where a photo was taken? A manually assigned location does not prove where an existing photo was originally captured. Live camera plus device location can record the device reported location at capture time, but this tool does not provide cryptographic or independently certified location proof. What is the difference between a visible stamp and EXIF GPS? The visible stamp is drawn into the downloaded JPG or PNG pixels. EXIF GPS is machine-readable latitude and longitude stored in JPEG metadata and may be read even when no coordinates are visibly printed. Does current location report exact accuracy? The tool displays the accuracy radius supplied by the browser, rounded to whole metres. It never substitutes a smaller estimate. Desktop and indoor locations may be approximate. Are OpenStreetMap tiles placed in my exported photo? The interactive tile layer is never captured. By default, the export uses a local coordinate locator labeled as a schematic, not a street map. Load street map optionally requests a static Geoapify image based on OpenStreetMap data; its attribution is kept in the export. If unavailable, the coordinate locator still works. Why is location search unavailable? Search and reverse geocoding use a same-origin Netlify Function backed by an optional server-side Geoapify key. The key is never exposed in browser code. Without that configuration, use the map, device location, existing GPS, or manual coordinates. Does metadata-only mode reduce image quality? For a valid JPEG, metadata-only mode replaces EXIF and inserts GPS without decoding or recompressing the JPEG pixel scan. Other EXIF is removed as part of the safe replacement. What happens when I remove GPS? The tool creates a separate JPEG without EXIF APP1 blocks. That removes GPS and other EXIF metadata while retaining the compressed JPEG pixel scan data. Are my coordinates or company details sent to analytics? No. Analytics receives only the established generic tool lifecycle event and status. Images, filenames, coordinates, address, accuracy, EXIF, company fields, remarks, logo, and search text are excluded. Location lookup and the optional street-map request send a query or selected coordinates through a same-origin function to Geoapify, never the photo or logo.

Delivery or service visits Label a permitted field photo with user-confirmed visit details without sending the image to the location provider. Location privacy cleanup Create a JPEG copy without GPS; the removal workflow strips all EXIF blocks while leaving compressed pixel scan data unrecompressed.

rows.description: Fill PDF forms and add text, checks, dates, images, or visual signatures over the original pages. Use it with GXA Toolbox.
rows.intro: Edit PDF fills supported existing AcroForm fields and adds text or visual marks over the original PDF pages. Fillable forms expose their actual controls; flat forms use positioned overlays, so the original artwork, page dimensions, rotation, order, and alignment remain the document base.
rows.howTo: 1 Choose one readable, unencrypted PDF up to 25 MB and wait for the original page preview Choose one readable, unencrypted PDF up to 25 MB and wait for the original page preview. 2 Fill detected form controls, or choose an overlay tool and tap the intended location on a flat page Fill detected form controls, or choose an overlay tool and tap the intended location on a flat page. 3 Adjust added text, font size, color, alignment, or image dimensions and review each edited page Adjust added text, font size, color, alignment, or image dimensions and review each edited page. 4 Choose whether supported form fields should remain editable or be flattened into their visible appearance Choose whether supported form fields should remain editable or be flattened into their visible appearance. 5 Download Edited PDF, reopen the saved copy, and check field values and overlay positions before sharing Download Edited PDF, reopen the saved copy, and check field values and overlay positions before sharing.
rows.faq: Can I edit existing text already printed in a PDF? Existing static PDF text is part of the page content and is not directly editable here. You can fill detected form fields or add text and other elements on top of the original page. The editor does not extract and rebuild the document. How can I tell a fillable form from a flat form? A supported AcroForm contains real field objects that the editor detects and presents as controls. A flat or scanned form may look similar but contains no such fields; use overlays in its blank answer areas. Which form fields can I fill? Supported text and multiline fields, checkboxes, radio groups, and dropdowns can be edited. Unsupported field types and dynamic XFA forms are disclosed instead of being presented as working controls. Will the downloaded form remain editable? Keep fields editable is the default for supported form fields. The flatten option writes their filled appearance into the page, removing their interactive field behavior. Added overlays become page content in either mode. Will text move when I zoom or download? Overlay positions are stored in PDF page coordinates rather than screen pixels. Zoom changes the on-screen scale; the export uses the same page positions and preserves original page sizes and rotation. How do I add a checkmark or date to a flat form? Choose the Check or Date tool and place the new mark on the intended page. Move it into position and adjust the text or size as needed. For a detected checkbox, use its actual form control. Is a drawn or uploaded signature a digital signature? No. It is an image placed on the PDF as a visible signature appearance. It does not prove identity, create a certificate, or preserve an existing cryptographic signature after the document is edited. Are my document and answers stored or sent to analytics? PDF bytes, entered form values, added text, and signature images remain in the local editor memory. This workflow does not autosave them to localStorage or a server, and they are not included in tool lifecycle analytics. Download your work before leaving the editor. Can I edit an encrypted PDF? Unlock the document separately with its authorized password, then load the decrypted copy. Edit PDF does not silently bypass encryption. Can I type in any language? The current export uses standard PDF fonts and supports their Latin character repertoire. Arbitrary Unicode scripts and complex shaping are not supported; unsupported characters must be corrected before export.
